note: The three ways a unit of the pixel sweep runs on a card. A worker takes the profile whose card memory range holds its card (minimum_card_memory_mb <= memory < card_memory_below_mb; null means no upper bound); the ranges do not overlap. It starts units of that profile only, and continues the units that started under a profile its own lists in `continues`. The learner and environment settings of the first two are the command-line JSON of the archived baseline of 2026-11-06 (its units/make_final_units.py): one copy on the RTX A4500, four copies on the H100 NVL. `archived_runs` are the archived runs whose copies, in order, are a profile's copies; a smoke job compares its first default updates with them. A unit keeps the profile of its first start; the settings used are written into its queue record then.

one copy.memory_note: One copy with these settings used 8.6 GB of card memory and 6 GB of host memory (RTX 5080, 2026-11-07). The 10,000 MB floor lets an RTX 2080 Ti (about 10,850 MB) take a unit; its speed check decides whether that card type is used.

four copies.memory_note: 75,343 MB of card memory on an MIT H200 and 70,013 MB on a Gautschi H100 80 GB (smoke jobs of 2026-11-18). Cards of 140,000 MB or more run eight copies instead (user decision of 2026-11-18 about 21:50 PT, "8 montezuma per h200").

eight copies.memory_note: The four-copy settings with the reset lane budget doubled with the copies (16 -> 32), which changes the speed only. Measured on one MIT H200 (143,771 MB), job 29603853 of 2026-11-18: 3.55 s per update against 2.17 s with four copies (22% more total steps per second), 122,787 MB of card memory (the 0.85 share JAX may take), host MaxRSS 12.1 GB; every copy's first update within the smoke rule against the archived run of its seed. The eight-copy numbers differ from the four-copy numbers at rounding level (524 to 531 of the recorded values over 60 updates), which the user accepted: bit-for-bit claims hold within one card type and one pack size. An eight-copy worker also continues four-copy units that started (on an H200 their four-copy settings use 75 GB).
